items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: luckily, George Salsbury, a piano player was there in the dressing room so I called George over, so George finished the gig for me that night.

ctx.x: They don’t fool around with that, did they?

No they didn’t fool around. The guy told me he says, he was real nice at first, we took intermission you know, and we took intermission and he says, “we’ve got some important business we’ve got to talk to you” and there’s two of them. They says, he says, “we’d appreciate it if you’d finish everything you’ve got to do, so we can get to this business.” So I kept fooling around, so they came back to me and says, “look I’ll tell you something.” They says, “We don’t want to upset you or nothing, but we’ve got — here…

items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: George Salsbury, the piano player there in Kansas City... I found Salsbury, so he told me he'd finish the night on piano.

ctx.x: George Salsbury, the piano player there in Kansas City. And so I called John to me and I said, these guys are taking me to Leavenworth. I says, talk to them. So John Termin talked to them. He couldn't make no headway. So John said, well, yeah, you're going to have to go.

I says, well, okay. I said, well, John, I tell you what you do. Now, look, of all the things that you do tonight, get that music and take it home with you tonight and keep it. He said, well, what about the band, don't you want the band to -- he says, 'we've got all these dates, ain't no need of missing this money. I can be sending you this money while you're in the service.'
